from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresher: The Complex Plane", [
            "Complex points act as geometric transformations.",
            "Squaring maps rotate and scale points.",
            "Functions transform the entire complex plane."
        ])
        
        # Assets
        grid_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/grid.svg")
        ruler_asset = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/ruler.svg")
        
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-2, 2], axis_config={"include_tip": True, "color": WHITE})
        plane_group = VGroup(grid_asset, axes).scale(0.8)
        self.place_in_area(plane_group, 'C3', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6)
        
        z_val = 1 + 0.5j
        z = Dot(point=axes.c2p(z_val.real, z_val.imag), color=YELLOW)
        z_label = MathTex("z", color=YELLOW).next_to(z, UP)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(YELLOW)
        self.play(FadeIn(plane_group))
        self.play(Create(z), Write(z_label))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(BLUE)
        z_squared = z_val**2
        z2 = Dot(point=axes.c2p(z_squared.real, z_squared.imag), color=BLUE)
        z2_label = MathTex("z^2", color=BLUE).next_to(z2, UP)
        
        # Ruler asset usage
        ruler = ruler_asset.copy()
        self.place_in_area(ruler, 'C4', 'D5', scale_factor=0.4)
        
        self.play(TransformFromCopy(z, z2), Write(z2_label), FadeIn(ruler))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(GREEN)
        self.play(FadeOut(axes), FadeOut(z2_label), FadeOut(ruler))
        self.wait(2)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Concept of Iteration", [
            "Dynamic systems apply functions repeatedly.",
            "Orbits track a point's sequence of positions.",
            "Iteration turns simple rules into long paths."
        ])
        
        # Define assets (Using generic shape replacements since paths are abstract)
        planet = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/planet.svg")
        satellite = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/satellite.svg")
        
        circle = Circle(radius=1.0, color="#FF00FF")
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF00FF")
        self.place_at_grid(circle, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.place_at_grid(planet, 'B4', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(Create(circle), FadeIn(planet))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(point, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6)
        self.play(FadeIn(point))
        self.wait(0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FFFF")
        
        path = VGroup()
        curr = complex(0.2, 0.2)
        
        # Animate satellite orbiting
        for i in range(3):
            next_val = curr**2
            
            # Map complex point to grid area (B4 to E6)
            new_dot = Dot(color=YELLOW, radius=0.05)
            # Simple scaling to keep it within B4-E6 bounds
            pos = np.array([4.5 + next_val.real * 0.5, 1.5 - next_val.imag * 0.5, 0])
            new_dot.move_to(pos)
            path.add(new_dot)
            
            self.play(
                point.animate.move_to(pos),
                satellite.animate.move_to(pos),
                FadeIn(new_dot)
            )
            curr = next_val
        
        self.play(FadeIn(satellite))
        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Fixed Points and Stability", [

            "Stability depends on the function's local derivative.",
            "Attractors pull orbits in, repellers push away."
        ])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#00FFFF")
        eq = MathTex(r"z = f(z)", color="#00FFFF")
        # Apply fix for Issue 27 and 29: Use place_in_area for formulas
        self.place_in_area(eq, 'A2', 'B3', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(eq))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF00FF")
        deriv = MathTex(r"|f'(z)|", color="#FF00FF")
        # Apply fix for Issue 27 and 29: Use place_in_area for formulas
        self.place_in_area(deriv, 'A5', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(deriv))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFF00")
        
        # Load SVG Assets
        attractor_img = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/magnet.svg")

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Julia Set: The Boundary of Chaos", [
            "Julia sets define boundaries of chaotic behavior.", 
            "They distinguish between convergence and escape regions.", 
            "Fractal fences separate stable and unstable dynamics."
        ])
        
        # Elements
        formula = MathTex(r"z_{n+1} = z_n^2 + c", color="#FFFF00")
        
        # Path
        escape_path = VMobject(color=RED).set_points_smoothly([self.grid["C4"], self.grid["C5"], self.grid["D6"], self.grid["E6"]])
        stable_path = VMobject(color=BLUE).set_points_smoothly([self.grid["C4"], self.grid["C3"], self.grid["D2"], self.grid["E2"]])
        
        # Asset fence
        fence = SVGMobject("/scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/fence.svg", color="#00FF00")
        
        # Group for placing in area
        group = VGroup(formula, escape_path, stable_path, fence)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFF00")
        self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0)
        self.play(Write(formula))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF0000")
        self.play(Create(escape_path), Create(stable_path))

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00FF00")
        # Placing fence in E3 and group in area as per reviewer feedback
        self.place_at_grid(fence, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9)
        self.place_in_area(group, 'B4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(FadeIn(fence))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Visual Synthesis", [
            "Simple algebraic rules produce infinite complexity.",
            "Deterministic systems create beautiful, chaotic patterns.",
            "The Mandelbrot set maps all Julia dynamics."
        ])
        
        # --- Visual Setup ---
        # Drawing a simplified fractal-like shape to represent Mandelbrot/Julia set
        # Using a set of concentric shapes for visual interest
        fractal = VGroup(*[
            Circle(radius=r, color=WHITE, stroke_width=2).shift(LEFT * 0.5)
            for r in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5]
        ])
        
        # Fix: Positioning the fractal properly as per feedback
        self.place_in_area(fractal, 'C3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.5)

        # Placeholder for assets - using simple shapes as asset loading might fail in headless envs if not present
        # Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg
        icon = Square(color=WHITE, side_length=0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(FadeIn(fractal))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREEN))
        self.play(fractal.animate.set_stroke(color=RED, opacity=0.7))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.place_at_grid(icon, 'B6', scale_factor=0.5)
        self.play(FadeIn(icon))
        self.wait(2)
        self.play(FadeOut(fractal), FadeOut(icon), FadeOut(self.lecture), FadeOut(self.title))

outline.topic: Introduction to Holomorphic Dynamics: Iterating the Complex Plane

sections.title: Prerequisite Refresher: The Complex Plane
sections.content: Briefly revisit the complex plane (z = x + iy). Explain that points are vectors and complex functions act as geometric transformations (scaling, rotation, translation).
sections.example: Visualizing f(z) = z² as a doubling of the angle (rotation) and squaring of the distance from the origin (scaling).

sections.title: The Concept of Iteration
sections.content: Define a dynamical system as the repeated application of a function: z_{n+1} = f(z_n). Introduce the 'Orbit' of a point as the sequence of positions it visits over time.
sections.example: A 'Digital Frog' jumping on the complex plane; where it lands next depends on its current position and the rule f(z).

sections.title: Fixed Points and Stability
sections.content: Explain attractors (points where the orbit converges) and repellers (points where the orbit escapes). Define stability based on the derivative |f'(z)|.
sections.example: A whirlpool (attractor) pulling the Digital Frog into the center vs. a mountain peak (repeller) pushing it away toward infinity.

sections.title: The Julia Set: The Boundary of Chaos
sections.content: Introduce the Julia Set as the set of points where the behavior of the orbit is sensitive to initial conditions. This is the 'frontier' between convergence and escape.
sections.example: A lush garden (stable region) vs. an infinite abyss; the Julia Set is the intricate, fractal fence separating the two.

sections.title: Summary and Visual Synthesis
sections.content: Review how simple algebraic rules (like z² + c) create infinitely complex fractal structures. Conclude with the beauty of deterministic systems producing unpredictable, chaotic patterns.
sections.example: Showing the Mandelbrot set as the 'map' that contains all possible Julia sets, visually representing the evolution of the system's dynamics.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The complex plane transformation animation (z and z^2) overlaps with the lecture text, reducing readability of both elements. Fix: self.place_in_area(complex_plane_group, 'C1', 'F6', scale_factor=0.6) (line=1, object=complex_plane_group)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: The lecture text is left-aligned in an area that competes for visual focus with the central animation, causing clutter. Fix: self.place_in_area(lecture_text, 'A1', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=2, object=lecture_text)
issues.resolution_note: Lecture text positioned at 'B1'-'F2'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_1] Problem: Title placement is slightly cramped; needs more vertical breathing room to distinguish it from the main content grid. Fix: self.place_in_area(title, 'A1', 'A6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=3, object=title)
issues.resolution_note: Title positioned at 'A1'-'A6'.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The animation of the point and circle occupies the center-right area, which can potentially interfere with the viewer's focus on the left-side lecture text. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(circle, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0) (line=61, object=circle)
issues.resolution_note: Used B4 for circle positioning to avoid interference with lecture text.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: The point is currently positioned at C2, which is too close to the lecture notes on the left, risking visual clutter. Fix: Line 67: self.place_at_grid(point, 'B4', scale_factor=0.6) (line=67, object=point)
issues.resolution_note: Used B4 for point positioning with scale_factor=0.6.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_2] Problem: Inadequate use of the grid space makes the animation feel cramped, failing to balance with the static text area. Fix: self.place_in_area(animation_group, 'B4', 'E6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=70, object=animation_group)
issues.resolution_note: Optimized grid layout and used consistent positioning within the B4-E6 area for animation.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Current placement of formula and derivative on row B causes vertical crowding and risks visual clash with top-aligned text flow. Fix: Line 56/63: self.place_in_area(eq, 'B2', 'B3', scale_factor=0.9); self.place_in_area(deriv, 'B5', 'B6', scale_factor=0.9) (line=56, object=eq, deriv)
issues.resolution_note: Applied place_in_area for formulas in row B to avoid crowding.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: The Attractor and Repeller labels are too far from their respective visual nodes, creating disjointed grouping. Fix: Line 72/78: self.place_at_grid(attractor, 'D2', scale_factor=0.7); self.place_at_grid(repeller, 'D5', scale_factor=0.7) (line=72, object=attractor, repeller)
issues.resolution_note: Adjusted positions of attractor and repeller elements.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_3] Problem: Poor utilization of vertical space leads to a bottom-heavy layout, leaving the top half of the grid empty. Fix: Line 56: self.place_in_area(eq, 'A2', 'B3', scale_factor=1.0); self.place_in_area(deriv, 'A5', 'B6', scale_factor=1.0) (line=56, object=eq, deriv)
issues.resolution_note: Improved vertical spacing by using A/B rows for formula display.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The animation elements are centered too far to the left, causing them to visually collide with the left-aligned lecture text. Fix: Line 55: self.place_at_grid(formula, 'B4', scale_factor=1.0) (line=55, object=formula)
issues.resolution_note: Formula positioned at B4.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: The 'boundary' graphic occupies the same vertical level as the lecture notes, creating clutter. Fix: Line 61: self.place_at_grid(boundary, 'E3', scale_factor=0.9) (line=61, object=boundary)
issues.resolution_note: Boundary (fence) positioned at E3.

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_4] Problem: Poor grid utilization leaves the right-most columns (A6-F6) empty while the left side feels cramped. Fix: Line 62: self.place_in_area(group, 'B4', 'F6', scale_factor=0.8) (line=62, object=formula_group)

issues.description: [VideoCritic][section_5] Problem: The fractal animation is centered on the right side but visually competes with and distracts from the lecture notes on the left. Fix: self.place_in_area(fractal, 'C3', 'F5', scale_factor=0.5) (line=1, object=fractal)
